entry.title: GitHub Copilot – August 2026 model deprecations [Closing Down]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot is updating its model lineup on August 31, 2026 to keep you on the most capable and actively supported AI models available. Six older models will be retired, with newer alternatives ready to take their place — offering improved performance across coding, chat, and agent workflows. A 30-day advance notice gives you and your team time to review any workflows or integrations that reference specific models and update them before the change takes effect.

Expected Outcome

By consolidating the Copilot model portfolio around newer, higher-quality models, you get a simpler, more consistent experience without having to navigate deprecated or lower-priority options. The migration guidance and notice period are designed to make the transition smooth, so your integrations and model policies continue working without disruption.

entry.title: Migrate GitLab Repositories to GitHub with GitHub Enterprise Importer (GEI) [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now migrate your GitLab repositories to GitHub entirely on your own — no Expert Services engagement or partner agreement required. GitHub Enterprise Importer includes a production-ready GitLab adapter, the new gh gl2gh CLI extension, automated preflight checks, and clear remediation guidance so you can run migrations confidently on your own schedule. The experience is on par with all other supported migration paths in GitHub Enterprise Importer.

Expected Outcome

Teams moving from GitLab to GitHub should be able to start and complete their migration without procurement delays, scheduling friction, or added cost from required services engagements. By making this path fully self-serve and generally available, more organizations can act on their own timelines while getting predictable, high-quality migration outcomes from end to end.

entry.title: Enterprise Security Configurations can be enforced for organization admins [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Enterprise admins can enforce security configurations across organizations and repositories, preventing both organization and repository admins from overriding settings defined at the enterprise level. This gives security and compliance teams a reliable, consistent way to apply mandatory policies at scale.

Expected Outcome

Enterprises gain end-to-end control over their security posture, reducing the risk of policy drift caused by configuration changes at the organization or repository level. With enforceable security configurations, teams can meet compliance requirements with confidence and spend less time auditing or correcting downstream overrides.

entry.title: OAuth apps can opt in to token expiration and refresh [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

OAuth apps can now perform token rotation using short-lived access tokens and refresh tokens, giving developers a straightforward way to meet security standards and eliminating a source of long-lived tokens. This feature is opt-in for existing OAuth apps and on by default for newly created ones, so app developers can test and roll it out safely.

Expected Outcome

Rotating OAuth tokens regularly limits the window of exposure if a token is ever compromised — any previously exfiltrated token becomes invalid upon rotation. They also expire after 8 hours, the same as GitHub App user tokens. Developers building OAuth apps will be able to satisfy security policies that require credential rotation.

entry.title: Token-type specific credential revocation and de-authorization actions [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

When a security incident strikes, you can now revoke specific types of credentials—such as all personal access tokens or all SSH keys—without disrupting every other token in your organization or enterprise. Organization admins also gain the same bulk revocation controls that were previously only available to enterprise owners, so you can respond quickly at the level where you actually manage day-to-day access. This gives security teams a faster, more targeted way to contain credential compromise with minimal collateral impact.

Expected Outcome

Teams responding to credential incidents will spend less time manually hunting down individual tokens and less risk over-revoking credentials that don't need to be touched. By bringing token-type granularity and org-level parity to bulk revocation, GitHub aims to reduce the blast radius of self-serve incident response and help organizations contain threats more efficiently. The result is a more precise, less disruptive security workflow for enterprise members, org admins, and enterprise owners alike.

entry.title: Expand the Triage role (edit issue title/body, transfer, convert) [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The triage repository role now supports editing issue titles and descriptions, transferring issues between repositories, and converting issues to discussions — giving trusted contributors the tools they need to actually manage a backlog. You can bring on community triagers without handing over push access to your codebase, keeping your source code secure while still getting real help with housekeeping. This makes the triage role genuinely useful for open source maintainers and teams that rely on community contributions.

Expected Outcome

Maintainers should be able to delegate issue and project housekeeping to trusted contributors without granting write access to source code. By closing the gap between what the triage role is named for and what it can actually do, teams can scale their issue management safely and with greater confidence. This reduces the friction of growing an open source project or a large team-managed repository.

entry.title: Hide closed sub-issues [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

When you're tracking a long-running project with many sub-issues, completed items can quickly overwhelm the list and make it hard to see what still needs attention. A new "Hide closed issues" toggle in the sub-issues pane lets you instantly clear completed work from view so you can focus on what's still open. You can bring closed items back at any time, keeping full visibility without the clutter.

Expected Outcome

Teams using umbrella issues to track complex projects spend less time scrolling past finished work and more time acting on what's left to do. This improvement makes issue trackers easier to scan at a glance, reducing friction for anyone managing work across many tasks. The result is a faster, cleaner workflow for staying on top of active work in progress.

entry.title: Convert a repository's Branch Protections to Rulesets [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Repository admins can now convert all legacy branch protections to rulesets in a single guided flow, complete with a dry-run preview that shows exactly which rulesets will be created, flags redundant protections, and surfaces any settings that don't map directly. Each converted ruleset preserves the original protection's behavior, and admins choose whether to activate rules immediately or run them in evaluation mode first. This makes adopting rulesets straightforward and low-risk, with no gaps in rule coverage along the way.

Expected Outcome

Teams that have been putting off migrating to rulesets due to the manual, one-by-one effort involved can now complete the transition quickly and confidently at the repository level. By removing the cognitive load of manually re-creating each protection, we want to accelerate adoption of rulesets as the modern, more powerful standard for branch governance across organizations.

entry.title: Rule Insights Dashboard for repositories and organizations [GA] [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The Rule Insights Dashboard is now generally available, giving enterprise governance and compliance teams a single place to monitor rule evaluation and adherence across every repository in their organization. You can filter by custom properties, view aggregated metrics, export data to CSV, and access everything programmatically through the REST API — no more stitching together reports repository by repository. Whether you're auditing a single repo or reporting across thousands, you get consistent, reliable visibility in one experience.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise teams can now track and report on rule adherence at organization scale with confidence, replacing manual, fragmented workflows with a unified dashboard purpose-built for governance. Bringing the repository dashboard to general availability and adding the new org-wide view means compliance teams spend less time aggregating data and more time acting on it. The result is faster, more accurate reporting that scales with the size and complexity of your organization.

entry.title: Org and repo levels API for AI Security Detections enablement [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now enable and disable AI Security Detections across your organizations and repositories through the REST API, making it straightforward to roll out the feature at scale. This is especially useful for large enterprises managing hundreds or thousands of repositories, where manual UI configuration is not practical. The API follows the same ergonomics as the code scanning API and respects your existing enablement hierarchy from enterprise down to repository level.

Expected Outcome

Teams can adopt AI Security Detections faster and more consistently by integrating enablement into their standard infrastructure tooling rather than relying on manual steps in the GitHub UI. This removes a key blocker for automation-first customers and supports broader, more predictable rollouts across complex, multi-org environments.

entry.title: Simplify AI Security Detection enablement by unlinking it from CodeQL Default Setup [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now enable AI security detections independently of CodeQL, so your team gets AI-powered vulnerability detection at the pull request level regardless of which languages your codebase uses. If your projects rely primarily on languages like PHP that aren't covered by CodeQL, you no longer need to configure CodeQL default setup first. This makes it faster and simpler to start catching vulnerabilities with AI on every pull request.

Expected Outcome

By removing the dependency on CodeQL default setup, AI security detections become accessible to a significantly broader set of development teams, including those working in language ecosystems that CodeQL doesn't cover. This simplifies the enablement experience and reduces the friction that prevented many GitHub Advanced Security customers from using the feature. More teams should be able to activate and benefit from AI-powered security coverage with fewer configuration steps.

entry.title: Adding AI Security Detections metrics to the Security Overview on the organisation level [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Security managers and administrators can now see AI security detection findings, resolution rates, and feature impact across all their repositories directly in the Security Overview — no need to dig through individual pull requests. This org-level visibility makes it straightforward to measure whether AI-powered security detections are working and to share concrete results with security leadership. Teams get a clear picture of coverage and developer response in one place, making it easier to evaluate and expand their security programs.

Expected Outcome

Adding these metrics to the Security Overview removes a key barrier for teams that have adopted AI security detections but lack a way to demonstrate their value internally. Security leaders and buyers gain the ROI visibility they need to make confident decisions about sustaining and scaling the feature across their organization. The goal is to help customers prove impact, support continued investment, and drive broader adoption of AI-powered security detection.

entry.title: Rule Insights Dashboard for organizations [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The Rule Insights Dashboard now gives enterprise teams an organization-wide view of how repository rules are evaluated and followed across every repo in one place. With custom property filtering, aggregated metrics, CSV export, and REST API access, governance and compliance teams can generate org-wide reports without manually stitching together data from individual repositories. This makes it faster and easier to demonstrate compliance and maintain consistent governance across large codebases.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise teams responsible for governance and compliance gain reliable, aggregated visibility into rule adherence at the organization level — not just per repository. By centralizing this data with flexible filtering and export options, teams can spend less time on manual reporting and more time acting on insights. The goal is to make org-wide governance practical and scalable, even for organizations managing hundreds or thousands of repositories.

entry.title: Suggested Labels [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The label picker now surfaces your most relevant labels at the top, so you can apply the right label in seconds instead of scrolling through hundreds of options. A "Suggested labels" group shows labels you've recently used alongside the most popular ones in the repo, each with a short reason so you always know why they appear. This makes labeling faster and more accurate, whether you're triaging a single issue or working through a backlog.

Expected Outcome

Developers and maintainers spend less time hunting for the right label and more time doing meaningful work, resulting in better-labeled issues and pull requests across the board. By reducing choice fatigue in repos with large label sets, teams can triage more consistently and keep their workflows moving. Over time, smarter label suggestions help contributors get onboarded faster and keep project organization healthy with less manual effort.

entry.title: Pinned Items — pin Projects, Views & Milestones to the sidebar [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Pinned Items lets you save up to 25 projects, views, and milestones directly in the repository sidebar, so your most-used destinations are always one click away. Whether you're tracking a milestone, jumping back to a saved issue query, or checking in on a project board, you get there without navigating through menus every time. Your sidebar becomes a persistent launchpad tailored to how you actually work.

Expected Outcome

Saved views are powerful, but only if people come back to them — and data from the preview showed that most users who created a view never returned to it. Pinned Items closes that gap by keeping the things you care about visible and reachable in the sidebar at all times. The goal is to make saved views, projects, and milestones a natural part of the daily workflow, not a feature people set up once and forget.

entry.title: Archive labels [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now archive labels to retire them from active use without deleting them or losing any history. Archived labels disappear from pickers, autocomplete, and suggestions immediately, so your label list stays clean and relevant — while remaining applied to all existing issues, pull requests, and discussions. Un-archiving brings a label back at any time, so there's no risk in tidying up.

Expected Outcome

Repositories with long histories tend to accumulate hundreds of unused labels that clutter the label picker and slow down triage. Archive labels gives maintainers a safe, reversible way to retire labels they no longer need, so contributors can find the right labels quickly. The result is a cleaner labeling workflow and less friction when organizing and prioritizing work.

entry.title: Path-based exclusions for push rules in Rulesets [Public Preview] [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Path-based exclusions in push rulesets let you apply file push rules only where they matter — protecting critical paths while skipping generated code, documentation, or vendored assets that don't need the same governance. You get precise, surgical control over enforcement without loosening protections elsewhere in your repository. Exclusions are validated at setup time, so misconfigurations are caught before they reach your developers.

Expected Outcome

Teams can enforce strong push rules across their repositories without creating unnecessary friction for paths that follow different conventions. By giving admins the flexibility to exclude specific directories, this feature reduces workarounds, support requests, and the pressure to choose between blanket enforcement and blanket exemption. The result is a more accurate and trustworthy governance layer that reflects how real codebases are structured.

entry.title: GitHub Advanced Security trials on Team platform [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Team plan customers can now try GitHub Advanced Security with a self-serve trial before making a purchase decision. This gives Team customers hands-on access to security capabilities like code scanning, secret scanning, and dependency review to evaluate the real-world impact on their codebase. There's no commitment required to get started — just a direct path to understanding whether GitHub Advanced Security is right for your team.

Expected Outcome

Customers on the Team plan can now experience GitHub Advanced Security firsthand, removing the guesswork from the buying process. Teams can make confident, informed decisions about investing in advanced security tooling.

entry.title: Arbitrary issuers and claims for federated credentials [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now authenticate GitHub Apps using any compatible identity provider — including SPIFFE, Okta, GCP, AWS, Kubernetes clusters, and more — instead of managing private keys. Configure any issuer and claims that fit your infrastructure, and use federated credentials to mint installation tokens for your app's installations. This gives every team, regardless of their technology stack, a secure and flexible alternative to long-lived private keys.

Expected Outcome

Developers and platform teams can eliminate the operational burden of storing, rotating, and securing GitHub App private keys by integrating directly with the identity providers already powering their infrastructure. By extending federated credential support to any compatible issuer, GitHub Apps fit naturally into modern zero-trust and cloud-native environments. The result is a more secure authentication model that reduces credential sprawl and scales with the diversity of real-world infrastructure setups.
